derived_results.claim: For M independent equal-probability strata of the explicit priority CDF q, the ensemble estimator M^{-1} sum [W_A/q_A]Y has the correct conditional base expectation even though ancestor draws are not iid.

The stratified one-step rare-event estimator has conditional variance no larger than iid multinomial priority sampling. It follows directly from total variance: the stratified variance is the average within-stratum variance divided by M, whereas iid also includes the nonnegative between-stratum variance.

Systematic priority resampling keeps the correct ensemble expectation when expected counts are Mq, but its shared-offset dependence is not uniformly variance-improving and can alias with ordering. Prefer independent stratification as the robust default for semantic/proxy-sorted frontiers.

Adaptive particle count M_t is unbiased if chosen from past information before current offspring are sampled: condition on M_t and apply the fixed-M proof. Outcome-dependent current-generation stopping is not covered by naive 1/M weighting and needs a proper random-count design.

The defensive q>=eW floor and W/q<=1/e ratio bound survive stratification unchanged, so the r118/r119 bounded-loss and certification controls remain compatible with this one-step variance-reduction layer.

engineering_update.scope: The expectation/one-step variance statements are analytic for fixed predictable q, base-conditional descendant truth and independent equal-probability strata. Multi-generation recursive SMC needs the full proper-weighting construction.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Do not infer multi-generation total variance dominance from one-step stratification alone.
Systematic resampling is not invalid; only blanket variance dominance is rejected.
Outcome-dependent random particle counts need explicit proper weighting.
Environment/tool proposal bias still requires separate trajectory P/Q correction.
